title: Define the intervention proposal contract
businessObjective: Convert grounded intelligence into a controlled, reviewable proposal without granting AI authorization authority.
technicalObjective: Define a finite ProposalGenerator contract for diagnosis, evidence references, confidence, recommended action, alternatives, affected systems, requested capabilities, risk classification, approval requirement, verification plan, rollback plan, and expected outcome.
architectureReferences: docs/architecture/source/Sri U-Thong Grand Hotel AI OS.md
assumptions: No production write, deployment, or live credential access is authorized.
Proposal generation is logically separate from deterministic policy, approval, execution, verification, and audit.
acceptanceCriteria: The schema requires diagnosis, evidence references, confidence, recommended action, alternatives, affected systems, requested capabilities, risk classification, approval requirement, verification plan, rollback plan, and expected outcome.
The contract distinguishes no-action, more-evidence, recommendation, draft, branch-or-PR preparation, and escalation outcomes.
A proposal cannot represent itself as approved, authorized, verified, executed, or production-eligible.
Malformed, incomplete, unknown-capability, or internally inconsistent proposals fail deterministic validation.
Required tests pass and independent verification confirms forbidden paths were untouched.
solEscalationTriggers: Any proposal field would imply policy, approval, execution, or audit authority.
Any production access, credential, payment, booking, RLS, migration, authorization, or workflow-correctness ambiguity arises.
rollbackExpectations: Revert the intervention-proposal branch and generated artifacts; preserve audit and verification evidence.

stateTransitions.reason: Added by GOV-032 to separate structured intelligence from non-authoritative intervention proposals.
